summary: Inbox «ПРОЦЕСС» column no longer renders the raw instance-UUID (or a bare `agent:` key) as the primary identifier on the operator's main screen (capstone T-0647 P0). New ProcessRef primitive (sibling of ActorChip/RecordRef, T-0648) shows the HUMAN process-definition name as primary + the source record title (via RecordRef) as disambiguator; the UUID is demoted. Server: listInstanceInboxTasks now surfaces processName (batched via the REUSED resolveDefinitionNames — not N+1) and recordId (from the started/next_task payload, tenant-scoped RLS via withTenant), threaded onto InboxItem.
deviations_from_adr: No ADR authored (P0 UI+enrichment task). Followed the T-0648 established pattern verbatim: batch resolver + kit primitive + honest fallback.

Record TITLE is resolved client-side by the existing RecordRef (lazy GET /api/records/:id, PDP/tenant enforced by that endpoint) rather than server-batched, matching how RecordRef is already used elsewhere (T-0648). Server surfaces only recordId; no new records endpoint needed.
friction_events: Worktree had no node_modules — ran `npm ci` at root and web/ before any gate could run.

anti-case-lock (rights-ui-anti-case + read-pdp-anti-case) flagged case-literals I put in NEW test lines ('Согласование счёта', 'e-orlov') — the D-064 denylist scans added lines under src/ and web/src/ including tests. Replaced with neutral non-case values ('Обработка заявки', 'e-worker'); gate green.

Root `eslint web/src --ext .jsx` mis-parses .jsx (react plugin/parser not applied from that path) and reports pre-existing false errors on unchanged lines — this is exactly why the project's web lint script is `|| true`. The blocking server lint (`eslint src`) is 0 errors. My ProcessRef additions introduce no new lint findings.

Agent/defer inbox rows carry `inst = agent:<uuid>` and `execName = raw actor` (deferred-inbox-store.ts:182/202) — ProcessRef humanizes the `agent:` PROCESS key to the task's own step/name; the unclaimed-defer execName resolution is a broader separate concern (out of scope here, noted for follow-up).
